$comment: Everything studio needs, by stage. doctor.mjs checks these; /founder:setup fixes the automatic ones in one approved batch and guides the manual ones one at a time. Stages are cumulative: ideas < build < showcase < graduate. 'when' limits an item to machines or products that need it ('service' means a product's product/services.json lists it). 'fix' is a command or {fn}, either for all platforms or per platform. In strings, {{key}} is a value from studio.config(.local).json; a manual line whose values are empty is skipped. An item with no 'check' can't be verified and shows as a reminder.

stages.showcase: Publish case studies, demos and content
stages.graduate: Run a real product with paying customers

items.title: A capable computer
items.why: Local databases, browsers and builds need memory and disk space.
manual: 8 GB of RAM works; 16 GB is comfortable.
Keep at least 30 GB free on the drive that holds your products.

items.title: Homebrew
items.why: Installs Git, Node, the GitHub CLI and FFmpeg on a Mac.
manual: Open Terminal and paste the install command from brew.sh. It asks for your Mac password.
Run the two "Next steps" lines it prints, so `brew` is on your PATH.

items.title: Claude Code with a Pro or Max plan
items.why: Runs every studio flow.
manual: Install Claude Code from the link.
Run `claude` in a terminal and sign in with your Claude account.

items.title: Git
items.why: Version control for every repo.

linux: Install Git with your package manager, for example `sudo apt install git`.

items.title: Long file paths in Git
items.why: Windows limits paths to 260 characters unless Git is told otherwise; deep skill and package folders break installs without it.

items.title: Node.js 22 or newer
items.why: Runs the studio scripts and every product.

linux: Install Node 22 or newer, for example with `nvm install 22` (https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm).

items.title: Heavy tools off the system drive
items.why: Keeps global npm tools off a full system drive.

items.title: pnpm
items.why: The package manager every product uses.

items.title: GitHub CLI
items.why: Ideas, backlogs and repos live on GitHub.

items.title: Signed in to GitHub
items.why: Lets studio create your private repos and issues.
manual: Create a free GitHub account if you don't have one.
In a terminal, run `gh auth login --web` and choose GitHub.com, HTTPS, and sign in with your browser.
Then run `gh auth setup-git` so git pushes as that account.

items.title: Your git name and email
items.why: Every commit is signed with them.

check.cmd: git config --global user.name && git config --global user.email

manual: Studio asks for your name and uses GitHub's private no-reply email, so your real address stays private.

items.title: Specialist skills (shipped with the plugin)
items.why: The research, board, design, marketing, sales, legal and support skills ship as pinned copies inside the plugin: nothing to download, and nothing added to your other sessions.

all: Reinstall the plugin: `claude plugin update founder@full-stack-founder`.

items.title: Your private studio workspace
items.why: Holds your ideas, portfolio view, lessons and settings, separate from the plugin.
manual: /founder:setup asks a few questions, then creates the repo for you.

items.title: Idea labels in your workspace
items.why: Stages like status:building are labels.

items.title: Routine helpers run on Sonnet
items.why: Keeps cost down: only hard reasoning uses Opus.

items.title: Python 3
items.why: Runs founder-cfo's unit-economics calculator, so the numbers are computed, not estimated.

items.title: TypeScript language server
items.why: Lets Claude jump to definitions and see type errors as it edits.

fix.all: npm install -g typescript typescript-language-server && claude plugin install typescript-lsp@claude-plugins-official

items.title: Context7 (current library docs)
items.why: Stops Claude coding against outdated APIs.

fix.all: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp

items.title: Design review (Impeccable)
items.why: Product UI design and reviews, and writes DESIGN.md. Its own plugin (it has an engine and tools), so it isn't pinned with the other skills.

fix.all: claude plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable && claude plugin install impeccable@impeccable

items.title: Browser downloads off the system drive
items.why: Playwright and Puppeteer browsers are several hundred MB each.

items.title: Playwright CLI and its browser
items.why: Claude clicks through your app to test it and record demos, and renders launch videos. Pinned to the version this release was tested with.

fix.all: npm install -g @playwright/cli@0.1.24 && playwright-cli install --skills -g && playwright-cli install-browser

items.title: gitleaks (secret scanner)
items.why: /founder:verify and /founder:showcase check that no keys or passwords are in the code or its history.

items.title: Docker
items.why: Runs a product's local database. Only products that list a database need it.

win: To keep its large files off C, run the installer from an administrator terminal: `Start-Process -Wait ".\Docker Desktop Installer.exe" -ArgumentList 'install','--installation-dir={{dockerDir}}\app','--wsl-default-data-root={{dockerDir}}\data'` (otherwise just double-click it).
Choose All-users installation with WSL 2; leave Windows Containers off.
Accept Docker's terms when asked, then in Settings → General turn off 'Start Docker Desktop when you sign in'. Studio starts it only when a product needs it.
mac: Install OrbStack (lighter than Docker Desktop): `brew install orbstack`, then open it once.
linux: Install Docker Engine for your distribution from the link.

items.title: WSL memory limits
items.why: Caps the memory Docker's Linux VM can take, and gives it back when idle.

items.title: A folder for videos, images and slides
items.why: Media is too big for git. A Google Drive synced folder lets you share it; any local folder works.
manual: Recommended: install Google Drive for desktop, sign in, and create a `Products` folder in My Drive.
/founder:setup asks for the folder path and saves it as driveRoot.

items.title: FFmpeg
items.why: Renders launch videos.

items.title: Video skills (HeyGen Hyperframes, brag), pinned
items.why: Demo videos and launch clips. Installed from their own repos at the versions this release was tested with, because they bundle fonts and music under their own licences.

items.title: Your own domain
items.why: Case studies live at yourdomain.com/<product>; demos at <product>.yourdomain.com.
manual: Create a Cloudflare account (free).
Buy your domain through Cloudflare Registrar: it charges cost price and handles DNS.
/founder:setup asks for the domain and saves it.

items.title: The domain's DNS is on Cloudflare
items.why: Free DNS, SSL and bot protection (Turnstile).
manual: If you bought the domain elsewhere, add it to Cloudflare (Add a site) and change the nameservers at your registrar to the two Cloudflare gives you. It can take a few hours.

items.title: Signed in to Vercel
items.why: Free hosting for your portfolio site and demos (Hobby plan, non-commercial).
manual: Create a Vercel account with 'Continue with GitHub'.
In a terminal, run `vercel login`.

items.title: A shared Supabase project
items.why: One free cloud database for every product's early-access waitlist and demos.
manual: Create a Supabase account with GitHub.
Create one project named `studio` (free plan, nearest region).
Run `npx supabase login` in a terminal.
Give /founder:setup the project's reference ID (Project Settings → General). Keys stay in Vercel, never in chat.

items.title: Supabase's MCP server (read-only)
items.why: /founder:listen reads early-access signups from the shared project.

fix.all: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref={{supabase.studioProject}}&read_only=true"

manual: In Claude Code, run /mcp, choose supabase, and sign in with your Supabase account. It is read-only and limited to the studio project.

items.title: Your portfolio site
items.why: Case studies and early-access forms are published to it.
manual: Build it with Full Stack Founder itself: /founder:setup-product portfolio "Portfolio", then /founder:spec mvp, /founder:design and /founder:build. Its specs cover the case-study pages, the early-access form and the shared waitlist table.
Deploy it on Vercel at your domain, then /founder:setup saves its folder as site.repo.

items.title: Cloudflare Turnstile keys
items.why: Free bot protection on your early-access forms.
manual: Add a Turnstile widget for your domain.
Paste the site and secret keys into Vercel's environment variables when /founder:showcase asks. Never paste them in chat.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.why: Where your case studies, carousels and posts go. You always post them yourself.

items.title: Google Drive, Sheets and Gmail connectors (optional)
items.why: Lets flows create the Content log and Pipeline Sheets and Gmail drafts directly. Without them, flows write local files instead.
manual: Connect Google Drive, Sheets and Gmail under Claude → Settings → Connectors. If they don't appear in Claude Code's /mcp, flows fall back to local files.

items.title: Vercel Pro
items.why: Hobby is non-commercial; a product that earns money needs Pro.

items.title: Stripe
items.why: Payments.
manual: Create a Stripe account, then run `stripe login`.

items.title: Resend
items.why: Sends email from your domain.
manual: Create an account and verify your domain (it gives DNS records to add in Cloudflare).

items.title: Sentry
items.why: Error alerts from production.

items.title: PostHog
items.why: Product analytics.

items.title: Upstash
items.why: Rate limiting that works across servers.

items.title: Apple and Google developer accounts
items.why: Publishing mobile apps.
